tool_input.commit_message:
Two things, both about the audit trail's integrity.

## A DES-072 correction against m-2026-09-10-001

Records two facts the trail did not show. The round-1 evidence entry was
written as `- name: PR #515 merged as 6f61406 — ...` and YAML discarded
everything from `#515` onward as a comment, leaving `name: PR` while
`status: pass` survived. The evidence was real; its description was
destroyed by the parser and ethos accepted it silently. That defect is
fixed in PR #517 (244b6c3).

And the reason the correction exists: I repaired that entry on
2026-09-11 by hand-editing results.yaml (865c015, merged c846910). That
was the wrong remedy — ethos-11fy's interim guidance names hand-editing
results.yaml explicitly as a thing not to do, and `ethos mission
correct` already existed as the sanctioned additive-only path.

Closing ethos-11fy on the back of it: the sole open P1, stale since
2026-08-07, describing a mechanism DES-072 had already shipped. All
three of its stated requirements verified in code rather than asserted.

## `command` and six siblings added to the audit PII sweep

Copilot and qodo both found that `promptBearingKeys` omitted `command`,
so a Bash command string was never swept and an address inside it
sealed verbatim into `tool_input.command` and `tool_input_preview`. The
defect is the inconsistency: send_email inputs *are* redacted, so the
system stated a protection and missed it on the largest free-text
surface in the system — `command` is 5,293 of all tool_input keys
across 224 sealed chunks, more than every other tool combined.

Surveying the whole tool surface found six more, each earned by
evidence rather than by name sounding prose-like:

- old_string / new_string (Edit) — the same bytes to the same file that
  `content` was already swept for under Write
- args (Skill) — carries whole prompts
- title / commit_title / commit_message (github PR tools) — `body` was
  already covered for those same tools; a merge commit message is where
  a Co-Authored-By trailer lands

27 keys correctly stay excluded as structured, enum, or numeric.

The existing doc comment claimed widening "can only redact more; it
cannot leak." True about leaks, silent about legibility, and now
corrected: `git@github.com` and a Go toolchain module path are both
address-shaped and now get rewritten — 13 false positives against 15
real addresses in this repo's chunks. emailPattern was deliberately NOT
narrowed to dodge that, because one pattern serves every key and a
carve-out keeping a clone line legible opens the same hole in a mail
subject.

Falsified at the binary level: the installed `ethos` is pre-fix code, so
the same payload through the same entry point shows the address
unredacted before and `[redacted-email]` after.

Sealed chunks are NOT scrubbed, and the CHANGELOG says so. Rewriting a
sealed chunk's bytes and re-deriving its hash is indistinguishable from
tampering; `ethos audit quarantine` is the path if one ever must be.
Not warranted here — those addresses are already in 11 tracked files on
main, including identities/jfreeman.yaml where jim@punt-labs.com sits by
design.

29 ok, 0 FAIL, race enabled.

tool_input.prompt:
One documentation-correctness fix on branch `fix/self-install-guidance` in <repo>. Do NOT push — commit and report; the leader pushes.

## The defect

Three places tell agents never to run `make install`, and the stated reason is false.

`docs/development.md:251`:
> **Never self-install.** Do not run `make install` from inside Claude Code. The ethos binary is loaded by Claude Code's process tree; macOS will not allow overwriting a running binary. Ask the user to run `make install` from their shell. Use `.tmp/ethos` for testing.

`internal/enable/guide/CLAUDE.md:78-79` and its deposited copy `.punt-labs/ethos/CLAUDE.md:78-79` (currently byte-identical — keep them that way):
> - Never run `make install` from inside Claude Code — the running binary
>   cannot overwrite itself. Ask a human to run it from a shell.

**The premise does not hold.** `Makefile:129-132`:

```make
install: build
	mkdir -p $(HOME)/.local/bin
	rm -f $(HOME)/.local/bin/ethos
	cp ethos $(HOME)/.local/bin/ethos
```

The `rm -f` unlinks the old inode before `cp` creates a new file. A running process keeps its own inode alive by ordinary Unix semantics, so there is no overwrite of a running image and no `ETXTBSY` — on Linux or macOS. The Makefile already does the exact dance that prevents the failure the docs cite as the reason for the prohibition.

Cost of the error, observed today: the operator had to run `make install` by hand to activate the PII-redaction fix from PR #518, a round trip that was not necessary.

## Step 1 — verify before changing anything

Do not take the above on faith; it is my reasoning and I have been wrong this session.

- Confirm the Makefile mechanism reads as described, and that no other install path (goreleaser, install.sh, a brew formula) overwrites in place instead.
- Establish whether `ETXTBSY` could still arise on any path an agent would realistically take.
- Check `git log`/`git blame` on that guidance for whether it predates the `rm -f`, which would explain how it became stale rather than being wrong when written. Report what you find either way.

If the prohibition turns out to be justified for a reason the docs state badly, say so and STOP rather than removing a guard that earns its place. A reviewer — or a leader — being wrong is itself the finding.

## Step 2 — the real caveat, which must survive

There IS a genuine gotcha nearby and it must not be lost in the rewrite: **replacing the binary does not restart an already-running MCP server.** `ethos serve` started before the install keeps executing the old code until it is reconnected. This repo already documents that shape for z-spec — "Reinstalling the CLI does not restart a running MCP server. Reconnect the z-spec server after `make install` or the old code keeps answering." Ethos has the same exposure and does not say so.

That is the useful warning the incorrect one was crowding out. Today's session is a live example: the redaction fix was inert until install, and a resident MCP server would have stayed inert afterwards.

## Step 3 — rewrite

Replace the false rule with what is actually true in all three places, keeping the two guide copies byte-identical. State plainly that self-install is safe and why (the unlink), and carry the MCP-restart caveat. Do not overstate in the other direction either — if you find a platform or path where care is genuinely needed, name it precisely rather than reinstating a blanket ban.

`docs/development.md` is the developer-facing doc; the guide is what `ethos enable` deposits into consumer repos, so its wording reaches every repo that enables ethos. Match each one's register.

## Gates

`make check` green with race. Report BOTH the `ok` count and the `FAIL` count. Pipe through `tee`, never redirect. `validate-content` has an embed-sync check for the deposited guide — make sure it passes rather than discovering it in CI. Docs-only, so nothing to falsify with a test; say that explicitly rather than inventing one. CHANGELOG entry under `[Unreleased]` only if you judge this user-facing; say which way you judged and why.
